name: Sheet-pan chicken fajitas
tip: Set everything in the middle of the table and let everyone build their own.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slice chicken and peppers into strips.

Roast for 20–22 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through in the thickest part. Finish with lime off the heat, tasting in small additions until the finished dish tastes bright and balanced.
Warm wraps and serve with grated cheddar and soured cream.

name: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled pork buns
tip: Start it in the morning and dinner practically takes care of itself.
method: Before switching on the slow cooker, pat the pork shoulder dry. Rub the whole joint with smoked paprika and crushed garlic, then set it on the sliced onion; add the BBQ sauce and apple cider vinegar around the meat. Slow-cook the joint whole rather than cutting it into cubes.

Slice the onion. Put the 1.2 kg pork shoulder in the slow cooker with the onion and about 150 ml BBQ sauce. Add 100 ml water if the cooker needs a little liquid; consult its instructions. Leave the whole joint intact while it slow-cooks and test for fork-tenderness before shredding into its reduced juices.
Cook on low for 7–8 hours, until tender and safely cooked.

Once the shoulder pulls apart easily, shred it into its cooking juices and simmer the sauce uncovered briefly if it needs thickening before piling into buns.
Fill six brioche buns with shredded pork and divide the 300 g prepared coleslaw between them. Serve extra BBQ sauce only if separately purchased.

name: Honey-soy salmon & greens
tip: A sweet-savoury glaze does all the heavy lifting.

name: Soft cinnamon swirl rolls
tip: A cosy weekend bake: allow time for two rises.
method: Warm the milk until lukewarm, not hot. Mix flour, yeast, caster sugar and a pinch of salt. Add milk, egg and 50 g softened butter; knead for 8–10 minutes until elastic. Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, then allow each rise to become visibly puffy before shaping or baking.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 60 minutes or until doubled in size.
Mix 30 g soft butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll dough to roughly 35 × 25 cm, spread the filling and roll up tightly from the long edge.
Cut into nine equal spirals. Arrange spaced slightly apart in a lined baking tin. Cover and rise for 35–45 minutes until visibly puffy.
Heat oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Bake 22–27 minutes until golden and cooked through in the centres.
Cool for 10 minutes. Stir the icing sugar with 1–2 tsp water and drizzle over warm rolls.
